rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with the provided 3BA label and image as an expanded blastocyst with B-grade ICM and good TE, but it overstates visible detail (e.g., flattened polygonal TE cells, imminent hatching) that is not clearly discernible in this single image.

Integrates age, PCOS, prior live birth, smoking, BMI, sperm parameters, and endometrial thickness into prognosis reasonably well, though some links (e.g., sperm effect on ICM grade, PCOS-specific embryo effects) are somewhat speculative.

The overall logic is structured and mostly consistent, with a plausible implantation estimate tied to embryo and patient factors, but several quantitative adjustments are heuristic and some causal claims are not strongly supported.

Core recommendations such as proceeding with single blastocyst transfer and standard luteal support are aligned, but suggestions like low-dose aspirin, ERA after a single additional failure, embryo glue/scratch, and broad PGT-A endorsement at age 32 are not strongly guideline-supported.
Provides clear practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including smoking cessation and future workup, though some recommendations are more speculative than standard-of-care.
